newsitem.title: CHINA: China to draw individual investors to bonds in '97.
newsitem.headline: China to draw individual investors to bonds in '97.

text.p: China will issue at least as much state debt in 1997 as it did this year and will try to encourage more individuals to invest in treasury bonds, official newspapers said on Thursday.
The Ministry of Finance would issue at least as much debt in treasury bills and bonds as this year's record 195 billion yuan ($23.5 billion), China Securities said.
Official newspapers said that China wanted more small investors to trade bonds to enliven the market.
Securities analysts said Beijing would try to tap China's huge reservoir of personal savings by attracting more individual investors and moving away from relying on institutions.
Personal savings in the banking system hit an estimated 3.79 trillion yuan at the end of October, official figures show.
China's economic planners have also looked for ways of keeping those funds out of the nation's stock markets.
"If they want to issue more bonds, they have to make the bonds attractive to all kinds of investors," said a Hong Kong-based analyst.
But that has some traders concerned that institutions will become sellers of listed bonds to make way for small investors, analysts said.
"The fear is that institutions are going to turn into sellers," said Zhao Xiaoyun, a securities analyst with China Securities Co.
He said small investors are still focusing on the nation's buoyant stock markets and bonds are seen as much less attractive.
